title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Are you an organised, detail-focused payroll professional looking for a part-time opportunity that offers a better work-life balance?

You'll support the smooth running of payroll operations, gain valuable experience and enjoy a working pattern that leaves more time for life outside of work.

- Salary: £28,000 per annum (Pro-Rata based on part-time hours of 5 hours per day).

Responsibilities in your new role as a Payroll Administrator

You will work closely with an experienced payroll team, helping on a range of payroll and administrative processes and developing your skills while helping ensure employees are paid correctly and on time. Your responsibilities will include: Your responsibilities will include:
- Accurately inputting, checking and maintaining employee information and payroll data, ensuring all records are kept up to date and compliant with GDPR requirements.
- Assisting with the preparation and processing of payroll, ensuring all information is accurate and submitted within required deadlines.
- Managing the Time & Attendance system, including processing timesheets, rotas, shift changes, overtime and absences, while identifying and correcting discrepancies to ensure accurate payroll calculations.

- Supporting the wider Payroll and People Teams with general administration, reporting, employee queries and ad hoc projects, including process improvements and business change initiatives.

Throughout your role, you'll be expected to maintain high standards of accuracy, professionalism and confidentiality while developing your knowledge of payroll processes and contributing to the efficient running of the wider team.

Your personality, experience and qualifications

You'll need at least one year's relevant Payroll experience, excellent English communication skills and a confident, organised approach to administrative tasks. You'll be comfortable working with numbers, handling sensitive information and maintaining accuracy in a busy, deadline-driven environment.
- Strong data entry skills with excellent attention to detail, numerical accuracy and confidence using spreadsheets and general office software.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills, with a methodical approach to work and the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, a professional and discreet approach to handling confidential information, and a positive attitude towards learning new skills and processes.

This part-time role requires working 5 hours per day (with salary paid pro-rata).

company: Three Bridges Recruitment LTD - Agency - Permanent
description:
Accounts Payable & Expenses Administrator

Glasgow £30,900 Hybrid Working 12-Month FTC

If you've built up good experience in accounts payable & expenses, & enjoy being part of a team where people help each other out, this could be an interesting next move.

We're recruiting for a leading law firm in Glasgow. It's a chance to join an established, friendly finance team, take responsibility for a varied workload & gain experience within a larger finance operation.

Although this is initially a 12-month contract, there's plenty to make the opportunity worthwhile, particularly if you enjoy working with good people, developing your skills & being part of a well-supported team.

What you'll be doing

You'll join a large team, working closely with the Team Managers & colleagues across the wider finance function.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing supplier invoices, payments & reconciliations.
- Managing employee expenses, ensuring claims are accurate & comply with company policies.
- Administering corporate credit cards, including monthly reconciliations for more than 300 users.
- Investigating discrepancies, resolving queries & following up outstanding transactions.
- Working with colleagues & suppliers to keep payments & expenses running smoothly.
- Supporting wider accounts payable activities & improvements to existing processes.

It's a busy role, so you'll need to be organised, comfortable managing deadlines & confident asking questions when something doesn't look right.

What we're looking for

You'll already have solid accounts payable experience, alongside hands-on experience of processing & administering expenses.

You'll also bring:
- Good Excel skills, including pivot tables, filters & formatting.
- Strong attention to detail & the ability to spot errors.
- Confidence communicating with colleagues & dealing with queries.
- A practical, organised approach & a willingness to get involved.

Experience in professional services would be helpful, but it's not essential. What's more important is your ability to understand processes, work accurately & communicate well with others.

What's on offer?

The Glasgow finance team has a friendly, approachable culture, with a relatively informal working environment & a strong sense of teamwork.

You'll also have access to learning and development opportunities, with the chance to broaden your understanding of other areas of finance.

The package includes:
- £30,900 salary
- Hybrid working, with approximately 50% working from home.
- 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays, increasing with service.
- Employer pension contributions matched up to 5%.
- Eligibility for a discretionary firmwide bonus of up to 5%, subject to firm performance.
- Private medical insurance, life assurance and wellbeing support.
- Gym membership subsidy and enhanced family leave benefits, subject to eligibility.

The team works together in the Glasgow office one day a week, with at least two office days expected each week. There's also some flexibility around start & finish times.

What happens after 12 months?

The role is a fixed-term contract while the firm considers its longer-term team structure.

There may be opportunities to secure a permanent position or move into another internal finance role, depending on future vacancies & business needs. Nothing is guaranteed, but you'll gain experience within an established international business & have the opportunity to build relationships across the finance team.

Interested?

At Three Bridges Recruitment, two of our values are "striving for brilliance" & "relatability". We want every applicant to receive an excellent experience & feel confident that a role is genuinely right for them.

If you're an experienced Accounts Payable professional with a good understanding of expenses administration, & you'd value joining a friendly, established finance team where you can contribute from day one and continue developing your experience, please apply with your most up-to-date CV or contact us for a confidential discussion.

description:

Location: Hillington Park, Glasgow.

KB Refrigeration is a leading provider of refrigeration, air conditioning and building services across the UK. With over five decades of industry experience, we specialise in the design, installation, commissioning, servicing and maintenance of commercial and industrial systems.

Based in Glasgow and working alongside our sister company, Carter Synergy, we pride ourselves on delivering high-quality, tailored solutions to our customers.

The Role

Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate the procurement of materials, equipment and services to support Service operations.
- Source materials, raise purchase orders and ensure all procurement procedures and controls are followed.
- Monitor outstanding purchase orders, track deliveries and obtain proof of delivery documentation.
- Liaise with suppliers to resolve invoice queries, delivery issues and discrepancies in a timely manner.
- Manage material returns, goods movements, stock adjustments and stock replenishment.
- Maintain accurate records relating to supplier accounts, subcontractors, bonded stock and free-issue stock.
- Ensure correct product coding is applied to support accurate reporting and financial analysis.
- Communicate effectively with engineers, suppliers, subcontractors, supervisors and management to support the completion of work within agreed service level agreements (SLAs).
- Prepare and update progress reports and maintain information on client systems.
- Support client-specific procurement and accounting requirements, ensuring processes are followed accurately.
- Maintain appropriate records relating to F-Gas regulations, including the documentation and tracking of refrigerant movements.
- Ensure legislative and compliance documentation is accurately recorded, filed and maintained.
- Provide general administrative support, including scanning, document management and maintaining accurate procurement records.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for a motivated and reliable individual who can work efficiently in a busy, fast-paced environment while maintaining high standards of accuracy and organisation.

The ideal candidate will have:
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities effectively.
- Competence using email, Microsoft Office and service management systems, with particularly strong Excel skills.
- A proactive attitude, excellent attention to detail and a commitment to delivering high-quality work.
- Previous experience in an administrative, purchasing or procurement role.
- A good understanding of procurement processes, purchase orders and supplier management.
- Excellent communication skills and the confidence to liaise with colleagues, suppliers and subcontractors.
- The ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team.
- A practical, solution-focused approach to resolving queries and meeting deadlines.

Why Join KB Refrigeration?

At KB Refrigeration, you will become part of an experienced and supportive team within an established business operating across the UK.

You will have the opportunity to develop your skills, gain valuable industry experience and play an important role in supporting the successful delivery of our services.

If you feel you have the skills and experience to succeed in this role, we would love to hear from you!

Apply today and take the next step in your career with KB Refrigeration.

title: Technical Project Coordinator, LED & Video Events
description:
Neo Recruitment is working with a Scottish live events technology business that delivers LED, video and graphics playout for major occasions across Scotland, England and Europe. They are looking for a Technical Project Coordinator who is as comfortable planning at a desk as they are troubleshooting on site.

The role

You will take an enquiry or a client handover and turn it into a clear plan, a clear job sheet and clear expectations for the freelancers delivering it. Then you will make sure it happens, mostly from the office and warehouse, and on site for the larger projects. It is a hands-on role with real ownership, and the standards you set will shape how every event is run.

Around 70% of your time will be based at the office and warehouse, and around 30% on project work, typically 2 to 5 day jobs. That includes travel across Scotland and England, and to Europe when a job requires it.

What you will be doing
- Building enquiries from a general concept through to project planning and delivery
- Turning client handover information, such as playlists, media assets and emails, into clear job sheets
- Creating production documents for each event, using lessons from past jobs
- Testing playout projects and distributing them to the teams who will run them
- Crewing events and managing freelancers on the ground
- Leading installation and commissioning across Scotland, England and, where necessary, Europe
- Tracking crew, subcontractor and technical purchasing costs, and supporting asset management in the warehouse

Who we would like to meet
- A technical background across hardware and software
- Good events industry experience, on site and in production operations
- Substantial LED and video experience, which is strongly preferred
- Experience of directing freelancers or subcontractors
- Practical troubleshooting skills and the ability to stay steady when events get busy
- Willingness to travel across Scotland and England, and to Europe when required
- vMix or live graphics experience would be a valuable bonus
- Based in or within commuting distance of the Glasgow area

If your background is in a neighbouring area of live events or AV and you have the hands-on skills, we would still like to hear from you.

What is on offer
- A permanent, full time role with genuine ownership from first enquiry to delivery
- Variety across the office, warehouse and live event sites
- The chance to shape freelancer standards and the way events are planned and documented

Next steps

Send us your CV and we will arrange a one hour Teams call: 15 minutes about the opportunity and the company, and 45 minutes about you. Your details are never shared without your permission. You must have the right to work in the UK.
